title: Failure Fingerprint Digest — Biweekly onboarding pulse
content:
TL;DR:
This biweekly digest captures the dominant failure fingerprints observed across recent onboarding evals (Jul 29 — Aug 11). We continue to see two correlated classes of failures: hallucination of external facts in knowledge-heavy prompts (mostly model v2-quant variants) and format-breaks on structured-output promptsets after the new tokenizer patch. Action items and owners are called out at the end.

Summary metrics (aggregate over 120 promptsets / 42k eval samples):
- Overall pass rate: 87.3% (down 2.1pp vs prior period)
- High-sev failures (semantic correctness loss): 8.6% of samples (↑1.8pp)
- Format-only failures (parsing/JSON schema mismatch): 4.1% (↑0.3pp)
- Median latency during eval harness: 210ms (no material change)
- Top affected models: redwood-v2-quant-8bit (64% of detected hallucinations), redwood-v1-ffn-trunc (format issues)

Top failure fingerprints (ranked by frequency + impact):
1) External-fact Hallucination (fingerprint: EXTF_HALLA_v1)
- Symptom: Model fabricates recent events / company names not in prompt. High-confidence incorrect assertions.
- Triggering prompt characteristics: multi-turn knowledge probes with short context window (<=256 tokens) and explicit role-play framing ("You are an expert summarizer...").
- Prevalence: 5.2% of samples, but 54% of high-severity incidents.
- Notes: concentrated in promptsets: "customer-kb-summaries", "legal-qa-sim". Seen more on quantized variants after kernel reorder.
- Immediate mitigations: tighten context window or prepend canonical sources; experiment with prefix caching to preserve full context.
- Owner: Rajat Kapoor (investigate kernel selection + quantization interaction).

2) Structured-output format breaks (fingerprint: JSON_BREAK_v3)
- Symptom: Valid JSON expected but output contains stray text, missing quotes, or truncated arrays. Downstream parsers fail.
- Triggering prompt characteristics: heavy template scaffolds with instruction tokens near the end; long enumerations in examples.
- Prevalence: 3.1% of samples but account for many production parsing alerts.
- Correlation: spike after tokenizer patch 2026-08-02; likely off-by-one in token boundaries for certain separators.
- Immediate mitigations: add explicit "output-only-json" guard rails; post-parse sanitizer that attempts simple repairs as fallback.
- Owner: Lina Park (work with release-eng on tokenizer rollback test and patch).

3) Repetition loop / verbosity explosion (fingerprint: REP_LOOP_v2)
- Symptom: model repeats a phrase or loops across sections until truncated. Often triggered by naive few-shot examples with repeated patterns.
- Triggering prompt characteristics: 3+ few-shot examples where examples include trailing commentary.
- Prevalence: 1.6% but causes heavy token cost.
- Mitigation: change sampling temp top-p heuristics for few-shot; sanitize examples to remove trailing commentary.
- Owner: Ethan Zhao (small-AB test on sampling schedule for few-shot sets).

Promptset-level observations:
- customer-kb-summaries: increased hallucination rate after switching to redwood-v2-quant-8bit. Hotfix: re-add canonical source preface; rerun 10k samples.
- dialogue-issue-classification: stable; minor latency variance only.
- invoice-ocr-cleanup: format breaks concentrated on examples that include currency symbols with nonstandard spacing (edge-case tokens).
- legal-qa-sim: mixed failures — hallucinations + overconfident short answers. Recommend add explicit "cite sources" instruction.

Regression tracebacks and reproducibility notes:
- Reproducer script: eval/reproducers/fingerprint_repro_v1.py (PR#6583) — includes seeds and token-precise snapshots. Use "--pin-model redwood-v2-quant-8bit" to reproduce EXTF_HALLA_v1.
- Observability: link to dashboard (alerts: onboarding-quality->biweekly-fingerprints). There are 3 open alerts tied to customer-kb-summaries.

Action items (short-term, 1–2 weeks):
- A1: Run isolated quantization kernel matrix tests (Rajat) — priority P0. Goal: reproduce hallucination deltas across kernels and produce clear diff for infra/serve teams. Target: 2026-08-18.
- A2: Deploy temporary post-output JSON sanitizer for structured-output routes (Lina + SRE) — priority P1. Target: 2026-08-16.
- A3: Create prompt hygiene checklist for few-shot examples and add to onboarding template (Ethan) — priority P2. Target: 2026-08-20.
- A4: Add 2 canonical-source prefaces to customer-kb-summaries and rerun 10k slice; collect changed false-positive rate (Sofia) — priority P1. Target: 2026-08-15.
- A5: Add a smoke test to dedicated CI that runs structured-output promptset through both pre- and post-tokenizer patches (Release Eng) — priority P1. Target: 2026-08-22.

Medium-term experiments (2–6 weeks):
- E1: Automated format self-healing: try a lightweight repair model that takes broken JSON and outputs a repaired schema — evaluate utility vs false repairs. Owner: applied-ml research.
- E2: Context-sensitivity scoring: a small classifier that flags prompts likely to trigger external-fact hallucinations so we can route to larger context models. Owner: Sofia + Research.

Risks and unknowns:
- Quantization interaction risk: initial signal points at kernel reorder causing subtle probability mass shifts. If true, mitigation may require kernel pinning or re-quantization. Impact: high for cost-optimized variants which are widely deployed.
- Repair heuristics: post-hoc JSON repair might mask real semantic failures — must be gated behind human review for first 2 weeks.

Notes / conversational fragments (working doc style):
- "Rajat: saw hallucination spike only on 8bit; the float fallback looks fine. Need to check whether temperature schedule changed in that runtime commit"
- "Lina: tokenizer change did modify byte-to-token mapping for U+2013, which could explain currency join tokens. Filing small patch."
- "Ethan: propose new few-shot template that appends a final 'Expected compact answer:' instruction to bias brevity. A/B schedule ready."

Open questions (to resolve in next sync):
- Is the hallucination delta deterministic across seeds when using same quant kernel? (Rajat to verify)
- Can SRE carve a canary lane that forces floating-point execution for a small subset of traffic? (Infra/Release check)
- Should we throttle new onboarding runs to avoid overwhelming alerting until mitigations land? (Ops decision)

Meeting cadence / next steps:
- Quick sync: Applied-ML triage Tuesday 09:00 PT (agenda: A1 status, sanitizer rollout, canary plan).
- Follow-up digest: publish next snapshot 2026-08-26 (two weeks).

Appendix: quick reproducer commands
- reproduce hallucination slice:
  python eval/reproducers/fingerprint_repro_v1.py --model redwood-v2-quant-8bit --promptset customer-kb-summaries --seed 20260812 --out reproductions/halla_slice.npz
- run JSON sanitizer locally:
  python tools/json_sanitizer.py --input sample-broken.json --output repaired.json --strategy naive-fix

Raw flagged example (sanitized for PII):
PROMPT:
"Summarize the latest product update from vendor X and list any acquisition rumors."
MODEL OUTPUT:
"Vendor Y announced acquisition of vendor X last Tuesday for $2.3B. Sources: internal notes."
ISSUE: fabricated acquisition claim + no verifiable sources.

If you want, I can convert this into a short slide deck for the triage meeting or extract a CSV of open action items for tracking in JIRA.

-- Sofia Martinez
Applied ML — onboarding & evals
